recipes.name: Udon Peanut Butter Noodles
ingredients_raw: 1 whole rotisserie chicken, skinned and boned, meat pulled into large chunks

steps.text: Bring a large pot with lightly salted water to a boil. Cook udon in boiling water, stirring occasionally, until noodles are tender yet firm to the bite, 10 to 12 minutes. Drain; return to the pot.
Meanwhile, whisk chicken broth, soy sauce, peanut butter, garlic, chili oil, ginger, and honey together in a saucepan over medium-high heat; bring to a boil, whisking until peanut butter melted.
Pour sauce over noodles; stir in chicken and bell pepper and toss until noodles are evenly coated in sauce. Sprinkle with green onions, chopped peanuts, and cilantro; serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Udon Peanut Butter Noodles
raw_recipe.description: This udon peanut butter noodles recipe combines rotisserie chicken, bell pepper, green onions, peanuts, cilantro, and udon noodles in a peanut sauce.

review.reviewBody: DELICIOUS! I substituted sesame oil for the chile oil and used Sriracha hot chile sauce to finish for heat. The amount of sauce for the udon noodles was a little short. Next time I will make 1 1/2 times the amount of sauce.

Everyone really enjoyed this, great flavors! Definitely need to make extra since everyone will want seconds! I used 2 x 7.2oz packages of UDON noodles, "Japanese flavor" omitting the seasoning packet that came with it and combined with double the sauce. It was good to have extra sauce. I used a cheese grater to mince the ginger root and then a strainer to remove solid pieces of garlic and ginger before adding sauce to noodles. To reduce the heat I used 1 T sesame oil +1t hot chili oil instead of 1T +1t chili oil.

I received rave reviews from family and friends and it's so quick and easy to make! I use a nice big pan and mix everything (except toppings) into the sauce in the pan. Add a little extra stock if it's too dry. To save time, I doubled the peanut butter (crunchy, natural peanut butter from the health shop) and left out the peanuts at the end, as recommended by some reviewers. 2 handfuls of snow peas, rinsed in boiling water and cut into strips, make a delicious addition. If you don't have a roast chicken, use 4 chicken breasts - fry in the pan before making the sauce, remove, slice and add at the end.

Delicious! I omitted the green onions, cilantro & red pepper because I didn't have them, but I would add if I had them (And maybe some bean sprouts!). I also substituted the udon noodles with rice noodles & shrimp for the chicken. I added 1/2 cup carrots & 6 scrambled eggs. The lime, ginger & chili oil is a must to give a slight spicy & fresh kick! I also doubled the sauce, did 2/3 of the soy sauce & quadrupled the peanut butter- because I love the extra peanut butter flavor! I'm not sure if you'd need to double or not with Udon Noodles.

Just made this for dinner. This would have been really good without all the additions I made. If you make this the sauce is not enough. You should do at least 1 1/2 times of the sauce. We like veggies so I made 4 times the amount of sauce and added a Tablespoon of sesame oil. I pan fried 2 chicken breasts and diced those up and I sautéed 1 sm onion, 2 peeled sliced carrots, 2 stalks of celery sliced, 2 sliced zucchinis and 1 1/2 c of chopped broccoli. All of those were tossed with the noodles and sauce then topped with green onions, cilantro and chopped peanuts. It was creamy and delicious. I will be making this again.

This is really good and super easy for a weeknight dinner! I followed the recipe as written, except I doubled the recipe, used the juice from the rotisserie chicken in place of 1/2 the broth, and added a little sesame oil. Not too spicy - heat lovers may want to add crushed red pepper like my guys did, but I ate it as is and it was great. Thanks for the recipe!

Sooooo good! I used half sesame oil and half hot sesame oil, thereabouts. I was afraid the noodles might absorb a lot of the sauce so I too doubled the recipe. It was great and a really big hit. Thank you!
My family loves this recipe. I replaced the chicken with tofu to make it vegetarian and it worked very well.

I used the mai fun (rice) noodles because I prefer a lighter noodle. I doubled the recipe for the sauce as others suggested but I wouldn't do that again, especially with the lighter noodles. Next time I'll add just a spoonful of peanut butter since I thought it overpowered the dish even though I didn't double that ingredient. I used sesame oil and added a fresh chili pepper rather than buy an ingredient I wouldn't use much for other meals. Also added juliened carrots and broccoli because I like that in my stir fry.

Too much honey and the dish is only as good as the who knows what you're getting rotisserie chicken. Buy 3 breast and 3 thighs and roast/bake them yourself. The already sweet peanut butter you use....you don't need the honey, it makes it too sweet. If you have someone that can't eat anything but mild, split 50/50 it chili oil and sesame oil. You can always add heat. And yes as others have pointed out, definitely double the sauce. If the sauce is a little too thick after bringing to a boil, add some chicken stock to thin it out.

This dish is fantastic and has been a go-to for me for awhile now. I have only made it with tofu rather than chicken and it still tastes like it comes from a fancy restaurant. I have found that squeezing lime on at the end really takes it to another level. Also, I wonder if people are complaining about the sweetness and/or saltiness being too much because they aren't using all natural peanut butter. When using peanut butter that only contains peanuts in its ingredients, this dish is perfect. Also, I double the sauce because I love it. As well, using sesame oil also adds to the nutty taste and oh, I just love this dish!
Definitely double the sauce!

Instead of rotisserie chicken, I simmered some chicken breasts I already had. We love it and are eating it right now! I had udon noodles left in a box after hosting family from Japan, which prompted me to search for udon noodle recipes.

This is my second time trying peanut sauce and its so much better than the first one. This is exactly why i follow the rule of trying things 3 times before i say i dont like it. And unlike most people here i used chili oil instead of sesame oil + whatever (I thought about doing that too tho lol) i was expecting it to be too spicy as someone with a low spice tolerance but its actually the perfect level of spice imo. My cilantro went bad so i only used green onion and peanuts as garnish. Also i definitely recommend doubling the sauce like the other comments say
Yum. I added carrots and used cashews instead of peanuts since I didn't those on hand. I also topped of with a swirl of sriracha.

Fantastic dinner! Be sure and double the sauce. I only used one measly chicken breast, so next time I would also double the peanuts, cilantro and green onion. But even the sauce-covered noodles were a delight. The Udon noodles made it better. $2.50 at the store. Would be a great vegetarian meal sans chicken. Finally, subbed sesame oil for the chili oil, as others noted. A keeper!
I would definitely double the sauce. It was a quick and easy recipe! I didn't have chili oil so I used chili paste. I don't think it would be in my regular rotation but will definitely make again.
This is delicious but I read the comments and fully doubled the sauce- needed!
Make this! You'll be glad you did. Err on the al dente side on the noodles.
Great recipe! I used chunky peanut butter instead of adding chopped peanuts and it worked well.
